# Arc TV 2.3.0 for Mac

2.3.0 adds an experimental way to find English subtitles, and Mac files are now named Arc TV.

## What is new

- **Experimental English subtitles (off by default).** If your source has no English subtitles, you can look some up from SubDL while you watch. Turn it on in **Settings → Playback → Experimental subtitles** and paste your own SubDL key (a free account at subdl.com). Use **Test key** to check it, and **Remove key** to turn it off and clear it.
- **How it works.** In the subtitle menu, choose to look up English subtitles. Arc TV searches by the title, year and, for episodes, the season and episode. You choose the release, and it loads like any other subtitle in all three players. Nothing is searched in the background, and nothing slows playback down.
- **Private by design.** Only the title, year and episode numbers are sent to SubDL. Your video, source address and stream links never leave your Mac. The key is never saved in ordinary backups or sync; it is only included if you choose encrypted backup secrets.
- **Files are named Arc TV.** Downloads now read `arc-tv-…` instead of `iptvnator-…`. Your data and settings are not affected.

## Good to know…

# Arc TV 2.2.9 for Mac

2.2.9 fixes downloading a whole season.

## What is fixed

- **"Download this season?" now actually downloads.** After you confirmed, nothing was added to the download queue. Confirming now queues every episode of the season, and cancelling or closing the dialog queues nothing. The same fix applies to the season and series "watched" actions that use the same dialog.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings are untouched.
- Android and iPhone are on 2.0.2.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.8 for Mac

2.2.8 brings smarter suggestions, a friendlier first run, and a sturdier database.

## What is new

- **Better suggestions.** The same title in different qualities now shows up once. Suggestions only include things your source can actually play, with more variety in each row. Brand-new viewers get sensible suggestions from their favourites instead of an empty page. Titles that are not matched yet can still appear, a little lower. "Not interested" can still be undone.
- **Clear setup card.** If Browse or For you needs TMDB or a built library, one card tells you what to do instead of dead tabs and filters.
- **A friendlier first run.** Home tells you what to do next, a source that cannot be reached shows a clear warning with Retry and Remove, and the Add source dialog uses plain words. "Source" and "favorites" are used the same way everywhere.
- **Easier to use.** Icon-only buttons have labels, and helper text and switches are easier to read in the dark theme.

## Under the hood

- Database writes retry briefly when the database is busy, so fewer actions fail under load. A failed library setup is recorded and Settings says so.

# Arc TV 2.2.7 for Mac

2.2.7 adds an optional way to match your library much faster.

## What is new

- **Faster matching (optional, off by default).** In Settings, next to the IMDb ratings download, you can now download IMDb's free title list. It shows the download size before you confirm, and you can remove it at any time. With it, most titles match on your Mac straight away, without asking the web for each one. TMDB and TVmaze are still used for anything the list misses.
- **Titles without a year can match too**, but only when the name and type point to exactly one title. Anything unsure is left for TMDB or for you to review.
- **Wikidata is used only when you fix a match by hand.** It cannot answer fast enough for a whole library, so it no longer takes part in builds.

## Good to know

- The IMDb list is IMDb's non-commercial dataset. Arc TV downloads it to your own Mac only when you ask, and never bundles or shares it. It is kept small by leaving out rarely rated titles.
- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings are untouched. If you never turn the new option on, nothing changes.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series…

# Arc TV 2.2.6 for Mac

2.2.6 makes Arc TV English only and a good deal smaller.

## What is new

- **English only.** The app language setting is gone, and the other 18 languages were removed, about 3 MB of translation files. If you had another language saved, Arc TV opens in English and nothing else in your settings changes. Old backups that mention a language still restore.
- **Content-language choices stay.** The language choices for movie and show titles in your library and recommendations are not affected.

## Under the hood

- Removed the translation checking and filling tools, and fixed an outdated logo test.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and other Settings are untouched.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.5 for Mac

2.2.5 makes Arc TV dark only and makes deleting data safer.

## What is new

- **Dark only.** Arc TV now always uses the dark look, and the first screen is black from the very first moment, with no white flash. The Theme setting is gone. If you had Light or System saved, it opens in dark and nothing else in your settings changes.
- **Delete all data also removes downloads.** Videos and partial files that Arc TV downloaded are removed from your download folder. Only files Arc TV recorded, directly in your Downloads folder or the folder you chose, are touched, and nothing else on your Mac.
- **No leftovers after deleting a source.** Deleting a source now also clears its catalogue entries, so a half-finished sync can no longer leave pieces behind.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and other Settings are untouched. Old backups that mention Light or System still restore.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.4 for Mac

2.2.4 is a tidy-up release: clearer wording, a few small fixes, and a lot of old code removed.

## What is new

- **Add source has a proper title.** The dialog no longer shows a raw label where its name should be.
- **Clearer Settings.** The backup export warns that a file with passwords lets anyone sign in as you. Restore says it replaces your current data. Delete-all and restore use the same word ("sources"). The Remote control row explains itself, and sync setup tells you why Continue is off.
- **Updates reads naturally.** It offers "Check for updates" first and shows a plain verdict after a check.
- **TMDB key check is clearer.** It now tells a refused key apart from a lost connection. If a check has just failed, "Build my library" waits until the key works.
- **One source is picked for you.** If you only have one source, Arc TV selects it, and the sidebar says "Select source".
- **Clearer backup message.** A backup made by a newer Arc TV tells you to update before restoring it.

## Under the hood

- Removed a large amount of old Xtream, Linux and Snap code that Arc TV no longer uses. This does not change how the app behaves.

# Arc TV 2.2.3 for Mac

2.2.3 gives subtitles a cleaner, smaller look.

## What is new

- **A compact subtitle box.** Subtitles now sit in one small, dark, see-through box that hugs the text, with white system text. It covers much less of the picture than before. It looks the same in all three players.
- **Smarter placement.** Subtitles stay just above the controls when they are showing and drop lower when the controls hide. Long lines wrap neatly and stay away from the edges.
- **Scales with the player.** Text grows in fullscreen and follows your saved subtitle size.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings are untouched, including your subtitle size.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.2 for Mac

2.2.2 fixes a blurred, empty player and an off-centre setup card.

## What is fixed

- **The video is visible again.** With Picture in Picture support on, movies, episodes and live TV could play (you heard the sound) while the picture was missing and only a blurred poster showed. The picture now fills the player, with all three players (the default, Video.js and ArtPlayer).
- **The setup card is centred.** On an empty Home or Sources page, the "connect your portal" card sat to one side. It is now in the middle.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings are untouched.
- Picture in Picture while browsing works as in 2.2.0.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.1 for Mac

2.2.1 makes **Build my library** much faster at matching titles.

## What is new

- **Matches show up sooner.** Arc TV now checks several titles at once and saves as it goes, instead of one at a time. On a large library, "matched" starts rising within a minute instead of staying close to 0.
- **See the progress.** The line now also shows how many titles were **checked**, for example "9,000 titles read · 1,200 checked · 400 matched". Titles that TMDB cannot identify count as checked, not matched.
- **Wikidata is skipped while building.** It answers only one request every 1.1 seconds, which held the whole build back. TMDB (and TVmaze for series) are still used. Wikidata is still used when you fix a match by hand.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings are untouched.
- Reading your portal is still one page a second, and TMDB use is still at most 8 requests a second.
- Android and iPhone stay on 2.0.1.
- Pick the **arm64** download on an M-series Mac and **x64** on an Intel Mac.

# Arc TV 2.2.0 for Mac

2.2.0 lets you keep watching while you browse, and makes building your library show results sooner.

## What is new

- **Keep watching while you browse.** Start a movie, episode or channel, then go back to look for something else. The video moves to a small floating window and keeps playing, so you can browse Home, Movies, Series, Live, Search and Settings without stopping it. Use the window's own back button, or **Return** in Arc TV, to go back to the full player at the same spot. Close it, or press **Stop**, to end playback. Starting something else replaces it, so there is only ever one video. You can turn this off in **Settings → Playback**.
- **Library results show up sooner.** **Build my library** now matches titles on TMDB while it is still reading them, so "matched" starts to rise early instead of staying at 0 until every title has been read. The status line says what it is doing.
- **One place for each setting.** The older duplicate indexing and details panels in Library are gone, and Sync stays only on Data. If you started the old indexing before, its progress shows in **My library**.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, ba…

# Arc TV 2.1.0 for Mac

2.1.0 makes the Mac app simpler: one button builds your library, and Settings is cleaner.

## What is new

- **One button builds your library.** In **Settings → Library**, **Build my library** reads your source's titles and matches them on TMDB, then keeps going on its own. You see one progress line, with Pause, Stop and Delete. It asks for your OK once, in plain words. If TMDB is off, Arc TV tells you what to do in one line. After you restore a backup, Arc TV offers the same button, so Home can look like it does on your other Mac.
- **Six calmer Settings pages.** General, Playback, Library, Home, Data and About. Remote Control now sits in General, TV Guide in Library, and Backup, Sync and Reset together in Data. Each row has a short name and one short line of help. Rarely used options are under one **Advanced** section per page.
- **No licence screen in the app.** Licences and credits now live in the README, under "Legal and credits". The app still carries the MIT licence file inside it, and shows one small TMDB credit line, as TMDB requires.

## What did not change

- Your sources, favourites, history, backups and Settings values are untouched. Old Settin…

# Arc TV 2.0.2 for Mac

2.0.2 lets a backup carry your catalogue index, so a second Mac does not have to walk your portal again.

## What is new

- **Include the catalogue index in a backup.** When you export, tick **Include the catalogue index**. It adds your portal's title list: names, categories, years and the portal's own ratings. When another Mac restores the file, it skips the hours-long catalogue walk, and the match decisions in the backup apply to those titles straight away.
- **No TMDB data in the file.** The catalogue index holds only what your portal itself reports. TMDB details are fetched again on the new Mac with its own key, so nothing from TMDB is copied between devices.
- **Off by default.** A large portal can add tens of megabytes to the file, so nothing is added unless you tick the box. It works with or without a passphrase.
- **Clear feedback on restore.** The restore screen lists the catalogue index with the other contents, and the result says how many titles were restored.

## What did not change

- Existing backups restore exactly as before, and the phones simply ignore the new section.
- Your data and settings are untouched.

# Arc TV 2.0.1 for Mac

2.0.1 fixes restoring a backup on a Mac that already has your portal, and the "damaged app" message on a fresh download.

## What is new

- **Fix a portal that will not sign in after a restore.** If your portal says "device_id mismatch" after you restore a backup, import again with the passphrase and tick **Use the device details from this backup**. Your portal remembers the first device IDs it saw, so this uses the ones from the Mac that worked. Without the option, Arc TV keeps what the Mac already has and tells you when the two differ.
- **A warning when a backup has no device IDs.** A backup exported without "Include passwords, device IDs and TMDB key" cannot restore the device IDs your portal checks. The restore screen now says so before you import.
- **Clearer export wording.** The option is now named **Include passwords, device IDs and TMDB key**, because the device IDs travel with the passwords in the encrypted part of the file.
- **The portal is selected for you.** After a restore that leaves exactly one portal, Arc TV selects it, so Movies, Live TV, Radio and Series appear straight away.

## What's new in Arc TV 2.0

Arc TV 2.0 helps you find something to watch, and makes your data safe to move. The Mac app gains a Browse page by
genre, an optional library index, better suggestions, stronger backups and an optional sync folder. Android and iPhone
gain Browse by genre with the optional library index, Up Next, a sleep timer, a channel schedule, an adult-content PIN, the same new backup file as the Mac and an optional sync folder. Android and iPhone are in early access, and the Mac is the main app.

Arc TV is a player, not a TV service. It includes no channels, movies or playlists. Your portals, history and settings
stay on your devices. TMDB, the library index and sync are off until you switch them on.

## Mac

- **Browse by genre.** Open Browse in the sidebar, pick a source, choose Movies or Series, and filter by genre, decade,
  rating and language. Sort by top rated, newest, title or recently added. It lists matched titles that have details in
  your library index.
- **Library index (optional).** Genres, year, rating and runtime for your matched titles, fetched with your own TMDB key
  and kept only on this Mac. It runs slowly, only while the app is idle, and you…

The phone remote's More menu works again: Search, Speed, Sleep timer, Full screen, Subtitles and the other tiles now respond to taps while a title is playing. After updating, reload the remote shortcut on your phone once.

**Phone remote stays connected:** when your phone's screen times out, the remote now reconnects within seconds of waking, keeps its controls on screen under a "Reconnecting to your Mac" banner (with Retry now) instead of going blank, and retries commands such as Search. It also keeps the phone's screen on while you are using it (up to 10 minutes without a touch).

**More reliable on the Mac:** a phone that goes to sleep no longer uses up the Mac's remote connections. The Mac now replaces the old connection when the same phone comes back, so it never refuses a returning phone.

**Its own icon:** the remote has a black-and-white click-pad icon, so it no longer looks like the Arc TV app on your home screen. Delete the old shortcut and add it again to see it.

**Phone remote fixes:** Episodes now opens the player's episode list in full screen. Use the dial to move between episodes, OK to play one, and Back to close the list before leaving full screen. The More menu gains an Episodes tile whenever there is an episode list.

**Simpler More menu:** the Controls tile is gone, because the dial already reaches the player's own controls. The Play, Episodes and Trailer shortcuts now show only while nothing is playing.

**A simpler, sleeker phone remote:** a glass dial with a progress ring around it, one control bar (Back, 10 seconds back and forward, Play/Pause, More), and a volume slider. Subtitles, audio, speed, the sleep timer, full screen, mute, next and previous episode, and search now live in a More menu that shows each setting's current value. On live TV the two seek keys become channel down and up.

**Speed and sleep timer from the phone:** both can now be changed straight from the More menu, with no need to steer the player's own menus.

**Ambient screen:** after 30 seconds idle during playback the phone dims to a true-black always-on style screen with a clock, the title and the position. A tap wakes it and dragging sideways seeks without waking it. The phone also stays awake while the remote is open. Scan the QR code again only if the remote shows "not paired".

**Subtitles:** captions sit a little lower in the player, closer to the bottom edge.

**Phone remote and player:** the arrow keys on your phone now steer the player's own controls, so you can set playback speed and the sleep timer (OK opens a menu, arrows choose, Back closes it). Trailers open from a "Play trailer" card the remote can press, and the phone gains Trailer and Controls buttons.

**Subtitles:** captions now sit centred at the bottom edge of the player, a little lower than before, and their panel is more see-through. They lift above the controls only while the controls are showing.
